rules.action: Treat the culprit lesion only in the acute setting. Stage non-culprit vessels after haemodynamic stabilisation.
rules.rationale: Routine complete revascularisation in cardiogenic shock does not improve outcomes (CULPRIT-SHOCK) and prolongs a high-risk procedure.
rules.detail: Minimise contrast load. Avoid lengthy balloon inflations. Delegate non-culprit PCI to a staged elective procedure.

rules.action: Prophylactic MCS strongly recommended before wiring. Microaxial pump preferred over IABP.
rules.rationale: Last remaining vessel + EF <30% represents the highest risk combination — any haemodynamic deterioration during PCI is immediately catastrophic.
rules.detail: Confirm cardiac surgical backup availability before proceeding. Microaxial pump preferred given severely impaired reserve.

rules.action: Prophylactic MCS strongly recommended. Establish support before wiring.
rules.rationale: Pre-procedural haemodynamic compromise in a last-remaining vessel case — minimal margin for intra-procedural deterioration.
rules.detail: Microaxial pump preferred. Escalate if haemodynamics deteriorate.

rules.action: Prophylactic MCS strongly recommended before wiring. Microaxial pump or IABP depending on EF and anatomy.
rules.rationale: No haemodynamic reserve exists if the only remaining vessel is compromised during PCI.
rules.detail: Cardiac surgical backup should be available and confirmed before the case.

rules.action: Prophylactic MCS should be strongly considered. Microaxial pump preferred given large territory at risk and poor haemodynamic reserve.
rules.rationale: EF <30% combined with LM or proximal LAD PCI creates high haemodynamic jeopardy — brief flow interruption during balloon inflation or stenting may not be tolerated.

rules.action: MCS should be considered. Discuss with team before proceeding.
rules.rationale: Severely impaired EF or pre-procedural haemodynamic compromise individually represent high-risk PCI features.
rules.detail: IABP minimum threshold. Microaxial pump if EF <35% or large jeopardy territory. Brief the team on MCS indication and access plan before starting.
